reviewer: Codex source inspection; not independent human adjudication
scope: All 11 INI records with fenodes in recovered training release

items.note: Addressee links to the isolated determiner A in s47. It does not identify an addressee. Do not repair it to Marx by intuition or count it as a valid counterexample.
The source links Perpetrator to They; the sentence calls them confederates in a crime. Exact participation versus co-perpetration requires semantic review. Keep the INI flag and link separate.

The sacked Position points to gardener in the same sentence. A job description is not a named individual; treating every non-null description as specific-entity hallucination would be a category error.
Employing Task also points to gardener. Role type, task description and token-reference recovery should be distinguished, rather than declaring any filler specific.

The exchange participant is linked to the devil in quoted figurative speech. The contextual relation must retain attribution and figurative scope; it is not evidence for a real-world devil transaction.
Undergoer points to She and the original annotation flags Uncertain_Interpretation. Do not treat this as an unambiguous DNI/INI test item.
Agent of the deed points to they in a would-have conditional. A supported participant in a hypothetical event does not assert that the deed occurred.
Killer of my murder points to they; context describes contemplated killing deemed too dangerous. Event factuality and argument licensing are distinct.
Speaker of threats points to they in s390; original Uncertain_Interpretation is retained. Cross-sentence resolution requires the surrounding narrative.

Prison of this cruel imprisonment points to my room in s392. The FE references two nodes in reverse XML order; surface order reconstructs my room. The natural passage identifies a location despite INI.
Perpetrator of crimes points to they in a may-be sentence. Scope includes possible crimes, not a factual assertion of one hundred completed crimes.
